To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the price of an anarchy for the stable matching problem is bounded by the square root of the number of agents, (2) the price of stability for the stable matching is bounded by the number of agents to the 2/3 power, (3) the average-case price of anarchy is bounded by the logarithm of the number of edges in the underlying graph, and (4) adding small switching costs to the model makes socially optimal matchings stable.

1) the social welfare loss from stability can be arbitrarily bad, but 2) under some conditions, it is bounded by a small constant, 3) under some other conditions, it is small on average, 4) under some other yet different conditions, there exist approximately stable matchings with small loss in social welfare, and 5) under some other still different conditions, decentralized partner-switching converges to approximately stable matchings.
the price of an anarchy of stable matchings is bounded by a function of the number of agents, the number of possible matches per agent, and a measure of heterogeneity of agents' tastes.
